title: So I've been making a beat 'em up set in a dystopian 2034 version of Porto. AI, pixel art, Godot, and a lot of trial and error
author: Friendzone69420
selftext:
Hey!

So, for the past 6 months or so, I've been working on this game called **INVICTA 2034**. It's basically my attempt at making an old-school beat 'em up / action RPG, but set in Porto, Portugal, where I live.

I've always loved those old 16-bit arcade games, and I figured, why not try making one set in my own city?

And I actually mean my own city. Every scenario in the game is based on photos I took myself. I've been walking around Porto with my camera, visiting the places I wanted to recreate, taking pictures and then using those as the basis for the game's backgrounds.

The game is set in 2034, though, so it's not just a straight recreation of Porto. The locations are adapted into a more dystopian version of the city. One of my goals is to eventually make the game a sort of playable tour of some of Porto's most amazing locations, except in a darker, messed-up future where people are trying to beat you up along the way.

The story follows Felix Vale, who's just trying to meet someone at a lighthouse. Simple enough, right? Well, apparently not. Things get complicated pretty quickly.

Oh, and you can pick up a bacalhau and use it to beat the crap out of enemies. I'm Portuguese. I had to.

Now, about the AI stuff.

I've been experimenting with Google Omni to generate character animations on green screen, then taking those videos into Aseprite and converting the frames into pixel art sprites. Getting everything consistent can be a nightmare sometimes, but when it works, it's pretty satisfying.

I'm also using AI to help with programming in Godot. Which is great until you change one little thing and suddenly three other things stop working. Fun times.

The music is all mine, though. I'm a music producer, and I composed the entire soundtrack myself. At least that was one part of the project where I knew exactly what I was doing!

Right now I'm messing around with the combat system, trying to make enemies actually behave like they have a brain. I want them to coordinate, react to what you're doing, and be a bit unpredictable. Making them hit harder would be easy, but that's not really what I'm after.

Anyway, after roughly 6 months of development, I've managed to put together a playable demo. There's still plenty I want to improve, but I figured it was time to get it out there and see what people think.

You can try it in your browser or download it for free:

[https://invicta2034.itch.io](https://invicta2034.itch.io/)

I've attached the trailer (I edited the trailer myself) so you can see what it looks like.

Would love some feedback, especially on the combat, visuals, and whether the dystopian Porto vibe comes through. And if anyone's curious about the whole AI-to-pixel-art process, ask away. I'm still figuring things out myself.

Cheers!
